descriptionAdvanced.en: The port of Puerto Quijarro is a vital commercial gateway located at the extreme eastern edge of Bolivia, on the banks of the Tamengo Canal. As part of the massive Paraguay-Paraná Waterway, it provides the landlocked nation with an essential sovereign outlet to the Atlantic Ocean. The port complex consists of several terminals, including Puerto Aguirre and Puerto Jennifer, which are specialized in the handling and export of soy, minerals, and fuel. Its location on the border with the Brazilian city of Corumbá makes it a buzzing hive of international trade, where rail, road, and river transport converge. Historically, it has been the cornerstone of Bolivia's economic strategy to diversify its trade routes and reduce dependency on Pacific ports.

en: Puerto Quijarro is the terminus of the Eastern Railway line that connects the border with the city of Santa Cruz.
The port handles millions of tons of agricultural products every year, destined primarily for markets in Europe and Asia.
It is located at an altitude of only 110 meters, enjoying a hot tropical climate.
The canal connecting the port to the Paraguay River is a key piece of regional maritime infrastructure.
